p0.original: 关键问题：我们如何通过操作性条件反射学习新行为
p0.en: Question: How do we learn new behaviors through operational reflexes?

p2.original: 在操作性条件反射中，某一行为引发的奖赏和惩罚等后果影响着该行为再次出现的概率。
p2.en: In the reflection of operational conditions, consequences such as rewards and penalties arising from an act affect the probability of the act being repeated.

p3.original: 通过经典条件反射，你可以教会一条狗分泌唾液，但不能教会它坐下或待着不动。为什么？因为唾液分泌是一种被动的、非自主的反射，而坐下和待着不动是更复杂的反应，通常是自主的。行为心理学家认为这种自主行为是由奖惩来控制的。因为奖惩在经典条件反射中不起作用，所以必由另一种重要的学习形式主导，心理学家称之为操作性条件反射。（顺便说一句，操作是生物体用来“操控”或影响环境的可观察行为。因此，如果你正在阅读本书以便在下一次考试中取得好成绩，那么阅读就是一种操作性行为。）你也可以将操作性条件反射（operant conditioning）视为一种学习形式，其中行为的后果激励行为改变。本部分的核心概念如下：
p3.en: By reflecting on the classic conditions, you can teach a dog to saliva, but you can't teach it to sit down or stay still. Why? Because saliva is a passive, non-autonomous reflection, sitting and remaining in is a more complex reaction, usually autonomous. Behavioural psychologists believe that this autonomous behaviour is controlled by rewards and penalties. Since rewards and punishments do not work in the classic reflections, they must be dominated by another important form of learning, referred to by psychologists as operational reflections. (Accordingly, the operation is a observable behaviour used by organisms to “manage” or to influence the environment. So if you're reading this book to achieve good results in the next exam, reading is an operational act. You can also see operational reflection as a form of learning in which the consequences of behaviour stimulate behaviour change. The core concepts of this section are as follows:

p4.original: 在操作性条件反射中，某一行为引发的奖赏和惩罚等后果影响着该行为再次出现的概率。
p4.en: In the reflection of operational conditions, consequences such as rewards and penalties arising from an act affect the probability of the act being repeated.

p5.original: 奖赏通常包括金钱、赞誉、食物或高分，所有这些结果都能够激励产生如上结果的相应行为。相反，痛苦、丧失特权或低分等惩罚也能够阻止导致此类结果的相应行为。
p5.en: Awards usually include money, praise, food or high marks, all of which can inspire the corresponding behaviour that produces the result. On the contrary, pain, loss of privileges or low-scoring penalties can also deter the corresponding conduct leading to such an outcome.

p6.original: 正如你将看到的，至少有两个原因使得操作性条件反射理论非常重要。其一，操作性条件反射比经典条件反射能够解释的行为范围更广。其二，它不仅解释了反射性行为，还解释了新的和自愿的行为。
p6.en: As you will see, there are at least two reasons why the reflection theory of operational conditions is very important. First, operational conditions reflect a wider range of behaviour than classic conditions explain. Second, it explains not only reflective behaviour, but also new and voluntary behaviour.

p15.original: 解释斯金纳对学习的看法。

p16.original: 操作性条件反射的创始人、美国心理学家B. F.斯金纳（1904—1990）的整个职业生涯都基于这样一个观点：对行为最强有力的影响是其后果，即行为之后立即发生的事情。实际上，这个观点最初并不是斯金纳提出的，他从另一位美国心理学家爱德华·桑代克那里借用了行为由奖赏和惩罚所控制的概念，后者用实验展示了如果提供食物作为奖赏，饥饿的动物会通过反复试错来努力解决问题。与巴甫洛夫的狗不同，桑代克的猫面临着一个需要自主行动的问题：如何打开“迷箱”的门来获得箱外的食物。猫的尝试起初似乎是随机的，但通过反复试错，失败的尝试逐渐消失，成功的行为被“留下”。桑代克称之为效果律（law of effect）（见图4-4）。即动物的行为带来想要或不想要的结果，从而影响动物是否会再次尝试这些行为。当你培养一项新技能如打篮球或玩新的电子游戏时，类似类型的试错学习也会发生。
p16.en: The entire career of the American psychologist B. F. Skinner (1904-1990), founder of the operational reflection of conditions, was based on the view that the most powerful influence on behaviour was its consequences, that is, what happened immediately after the act. Indeed, this view was not originally put forward by Skinner, who borrowed the concept of behaviour controlled by rewards and penalties from another American psychologist, Edward Sandeicker, who used experiments to show that hungry animals would try to solve problems by repeatedly testing faults if food was provided as a reward. Unlike Pavlov's dog, Sandek's cat is faced with a problem that needs to be acted upon: how to open the box door to get food outside the box. The cat's attempt initially seemed random, but through repeated error, the failed attempt gradually disappeared and successful behaviour was “remained”. Sandek refers to it as the law of effect (see figure 4-4). That is, the behaviour of animals produces desired or unwanted results, thus affecting whether animals will try these acts again. A similar type of mislearning occurs when you develop a new skill such as basketball or new video games.

p18.original: 注：迷箱测试了动物通过自主行动解决问题的能力。当某个行为取得成功时（当门打开、动物获得食物时），它们在随后的试次中会使用这种策略。这种建立在先前试次结果基础上的行为变化被称为效果律。
p18.en: Note: The box tested the ability of animals to solve problems through autonomous action. When an act succeeds (when the door is opened and the animal gets food), they will use this strategy in subsequent trials. This behavioural change, based on the previous test results, is referred to as the law of effect.

p19.original: 然而，斯金纳对桑代克的心理学所做的第一件事是摆脱对生物体感受、意图或目标的主观和不科学的推测。动物“想要”什么或它感受到的“快乐”对于客观理解动物的行为并不重要。作为一个激进的行为主义者，斯金纳拒绝考虑生物体大脑中发生的事情，因为这种推测无法通过观察来验证，而研究任何无法直接观察到的东西都会威胁到这个新兴心理学领域的科学可信度。例如，我们能够观察到进食，但无法观察到饥饿、渴求食物或进食时的愉悦等内在体验。因此，根据斯金纳的说法，我们可以观察到有人在吃东西，但我们不能仅凭观察就对他们是饿了还是享受进食做出任何假定。
p19.en: However, the first thing Skinner did about the psychology of Sandeiker was to get away from subjective and unscientific speculation about the feelings, intentions or objectives of organisms. An animal's “wanted” or its sense of “happy” is not important for an objective understanding of animal behaviour. As a radical activist, Skinner refuses to consider what is happening in the brain of a living organism, because this speculation cannot be verified by observation, and studying anything that cannot be directly observed threatens the scientific credibility of this emerging area of psychology. For example, we can observe food consumption, but cannot observe the inherent experiences of hunger, thirst for food or pleasure when eating. So, according to Skinner, we can observe people eating, but we cannot assume whether they are hungry or enjoying food on the basis of observation alone.

p22.original: 审视强化塑造我们行为的方式。
p22.en: To look at ways to strengthen the way we shape our behaviour.

p23.original: 斯金纳热切地想将行为主义确立为一门合法科学，这种热情渗透在他的工作之中。例如，虽然我们经常在日常对话中提到“奖赏”这个词，但斯金纳偏好使用更客观的术语“强化物”。为什么对术语的使用耿耿于怀？斯金纳反对使用“奖赏”这个词，理由是奖赏意味着接受者感到愉悦，而愉悦假定了我们了解生物体的内在体验，这对于斯金纳来说是绝不会考虑的。再者，强化物作用于可直接观察到的行为（而不是生物体的思想）（Winn，2001）。因此，斯金纳将强化物（reinforcer）定义为任何跟随在某个反应之后，并加强该反应的刺激。对于多数人来说，食物、金钱和性都起到了这样的作用。关注、赞美或微笑也是如此。所有这些都是正强化（positive reinforcement）的例子，通过在反应后添加正性刺激来加强反应，使行为更有可能再次发生。
p23.en: Skinner was keen to establish behaviorism as a legitimate science, and that enthusiasm permeated his work. For example, while the word “reward” is often mentioned in our daily dialogue, Skinner prefers to use a more objective term “enhanced”. Why is the use of terms so obscuring? Skinner is opposed to the word “reward” on the grounds that reward means pleasure to the recipient, and pleasure assumes that we know the inner experience of living organisms, which Skinner would never consider. Moreover, the reinforcements act on directly observable behaviour (rather than the idea of living organisms) (Winn, 2001). Therefore, Skinner defines reinforcement as any follow-up to a reaction and enhances its irritation. For most people, food, money and sex play such a role. The same applies to attention, praise or smile. All of these are examples of strengthened behaviour that enhances response by adding positive incentives to the response, making behaviour more likely to recur.

p24.original: 大多数人都知道与正强化相关的方法，但很少有人了解加强操作性反应的另一种主要方法：通过消除令人不快或厌恶的刺激来强化行为。心理学家称之为负强化（negative reinforcement）。（这里的负是数学意义上的减或消除，而正指的是加或施加。请不要像常见错误一样混淆负强化与惩罚；记住强化总是会增强行为，而惩罚——我们稍后讨论——会削弱它。）因此，在倾盆大雨中使用雨伞避免被淋湿是一种通过负强化来学习和维持的行为；也就是说，你使用雨伞来避免或消除令人不快的刺激（被淋湿）。同样，当你扣上安全带以阻止车内的安全带蜂鸣器发出恼人的声音时，你正是在接受负强化。现在花几分钟在你的笔记中标出负强化与惩罚之间的区别，将帮助你避免在考试中无法回答相应问题的不愉快，这个例子再次证明负强化具有加强行为的威力！
p24.en: Most people know the methods associated with strengthening, but few know another major way to strengthen operational responses: to strengthen behaviour by eliminating unpleasant or repugnant incentives. Psychologists call it negative reinforcement. (The negative here is a mathematical reduction or elimination, and it is the addition or imposition. Please do not confuse responsibilities with punishments as often as common mistakes. Remember that strengthening will always strengthen behaviour and punishment — we will discuss later — will weaken it. Thus, the use of umbrellas in pouring rain to avoid wetting is an act of learning and maintaining through negative reinforcement; In other words, you use umbrellas to avoid or eliminate unpleasant irritation. Again, when you put your seat belt on to stop the sound of the seat belt beeper in the car, you're receiving negative reinforcements. Now it will take a few minutes to mark the difference between negative reinforcement and punishment in your notes, and help you avoid the unpleasantness of being unable to answer the corresponding questions in your exams, an example that once again proves the power of enhanced behaviour!

p26.original: B. F.斯金纳（1956）的创新之一是发明了一种专用于研究强化物如何影响实验动物的简单装置：一个带有杠杆的盒子，动物可以通过按下杠杆来获得食物。他称这个装置为操作室（operant chamber）。（几乎所有人都称之为“斯金纳箱”，但斯金纳讨厌这个词。）通过设定一个封闭空间在某个杠杆被按下或某个灯被啄（对于斯金纳最喜欢的实验动物鸽子而言）的时候分发食物，动物很快就学会了获取食物所需的行为。自其发明以来，数以千计的心理学家和心理学专业的学生使用该仪器来研究操作性条件反射。斯金纳也使用这种封闭空间的变体来训练动物做出其他行为。其中一个著名的实验显示，一些聪明的鸽子也能玩人类喜欢的游戏。
p26.en: One of the innovations of B. F. Skinner (1956) was the creation of a simple device designed to study how the strengthening affects experimental animals: a box with leverage, through which animals can obtain food. He called it the operating room. (Almost everyone calls it the Skinner Box, but Skinner hates the word. By setting a closed space for food distribution when a lever is pressed or a lamp is pecked (for Skinner's favorite experimental animal pigeon), animals quickly learn the behaviour needed to obtain food. Since its creation, thousands of psychologists and students in psychology have used the instrument to study operational reflexes. Skinner also uses this closed-space variant to train animals to perform other acts. One of the famous experiments shows that some smart pigeons can play games that people like.

p27.original: 如果鸽子能学会打乒乓球，我们打赌你也可以教会你的宠物一些有用的行为。为了帮助你更多地了解你的宠物、孩子、室友或你自己的条件反射行为，让我们来了解操作性条件反射的一些细节。
p27.en: If pigeons learn to play ping-pong, we bet you can teach your pets some useful behavior. In order to help you learn more about your pets, children, roommates or your own condition reflexes, let's get some details about the operational reflexes.

p28.original: 漫画中的这个孩子因为哭泣而被允许与爸爸妈妈一起睡，这构成了孩子的正强化。具有讽刺意味的是，当父母让孩子睡在他们的床上以避免被哭泣的婴儿打扰时，这对于父母来说是一种负强化。
p28.en: The child in the comic book was allowed to sleep with his parents because of his crying, which constitutes a positive strengthening of the child. Ironically, this is a negative reinforcement for parents when parents leave their children to sleep in their beds to avoid being disturbed by crying babies.

p30.original: 在强化对行为的影响中，时间和频率起着关键作用。因此，虽然每年提供两三次成绩报告可能会适度强化大学生去学习，但这种不频繁的强化程序对日常学习习惯几乎没有影响（正如你所看到的）。许多教授当然意识到了这一点，于是在整个课程期间安排考试和作业并定期给出成绩。通过这种方式，他们鼓励学生连续学习，而不希望学生只在学期末临时抱佛脚。这是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，但还不够好。
p30.en: Time and frequency play a key role in enhancing the impact on behaviour. Thus, while the provision of two or three reports of achievement each year may moderately strengthen university students ' learning, this low-intensity process has little impact on daily learning habits (as you can see). Many professors were of course aware of this, so they arranged examinations and assignments and gave regular results throughout the course. In this way, they encourage students to continue their studies without wishing that they will only temporarily hold their feet at the end of the school year. This is a step in the right direction, but not good enough.

p31.original: 无论我们是在谈论大学生、《财富》杂志评出的500强企业的首席执行官（CEO）还是实验室大鼠，任何影响操作性学习的计划都需要仔细关注奖赏的时间和频率。
p31.en: Whether we're talking about college students, CEOs of the 500 companies of Fortune or lab rats, any plan to influence operational learning requires careful attention to the timing and frequency of rewards.

p32.original: 接受强化的对象要多久接受一次强化？
p32.en: How often do those receiving reinforcements receive reinforcements?

p33.original: 接受强化的对象必须做多少工作才能获得强化？
p33.en: How much work must be done by the recipients of the reinforcement to be strengthened?

p34.original: 接受强化的对象会在每次反应后都得到强化还是仅在一定数量的反应后才得到强化？
p34.en: Will the recipients be reinforced after each reaction or only after a certain number of responses?

p35.original: 正如你将看到的，这些决定将产生重大影响。
p35.en: As you will see, these decisions will have a significant impact.

p37.original: 假设你想教你的狗一项技能，例如，听从指挥。根据行为原则，你应该在开始训练计划时就对每一个正确的反应给予奖赏。心理学家称之为连续强化（continuous reinforcement）。这在学习过程的早期是一种有用的策略，因为奖赏每一个正确的反应、同时忽略不正确的反应，这为反应是否合乎期许提供了快速而清晰的反馈。
p37.en: Suppose you want to teach your dog a skill, for example, to follow command. In accordance with the principle of conduct, you should reward every right response when you start training programmes. Psychologists call it continuous reinforcement. This is a useful strategy at an early stage in the learning process, as rewards each correct response while ignoring incorrect responses provide quick and clear feedback on whether the response is adequate.

p38.original: 此外，连续强化有助于塑造复杂的新行为。塑造（shaping）常用于动物训练，包括有意使用奖赏（有时是惩罚）来鼓励越来越接近期望的行为。例如，在教狗坐下时，你可能会先说：“坐！”并同时帮助狗摆出坐姿，继而提供强化。不久，狗会在没有帮助的情况下独自坐下以获得强化。你一定在学校里经历过塑造，就像老师通过逐渐设定更高的标准来教你阅读、写作或演奏乐器。通过塑造，老师可以不断“提高标准”或提高获得奖赏所需的表现水平。总体来说，我们可以说连续强化是发展和塑造新行为的好策略。
p38.en: In addition, continuous intensification helps to shape complex new behaviour. Shaping is often used for animal training, including the deliberate use of rewards (sometimes punishments) to encourage behaviour closer to expectations. For example, when teaching dogs to sit, you might say, "Sit!" "and also help the dog to sit and then provide reinforcement. Soon the dog will sit alone without help to get reinforced. You must have been shaped in school, like a teacher who's been teaching you to read, write or play instruments by setting higher standards. By shaping them, teachers can constantly “uplift the standards” or increase the level of performance required to be rewarded. Overall, we can say that continuous reinforcement is a good strategy for developing and shaping new behaviour.

p39.original: 专注和持之以恒是成功的关键，即你必须在目标行为完成后立即进行强化。未能为正确反应提供奖赏很容易被学习者误解为其反应不正确。另一个关键点是强化物本身，如果过度使用，它会因学习者获得了过分满足而失去激励的效力。在这种情况下，训练员可能会等到接近喂食时间才塑造行为，以确保狗保持饥饿的状态并为了食物而工作。解决这个问题的一个好方法是只提供少量的强化物（刚好足以使它有意义），或者使用多种特定强化物并每次都换着使用它们。
p39.en: Focus and perseverance are key to success, namely, that you must strengthen yourself as soon as the targeted behaviour is completed. Failure to provide rewards for the correct response can be easily misunderstood by the learners for their incorrect response. Another key point is the strengthening itself, which, if overused, loses its incentive effect because the learners are oversatisfied. In such cases, trainers may wait until close to feeding hours to shape behaviour to ensure that dogs remain hungry and work for food. A good solution to this problem would be to provide only a small amount of reinforcements (which would be sufficient to make it meaningful), or to use a wide range of specific reinforcements and to use them in exchange each time.

p40.original: 一旦期望的行为形成（例如，当你的狗学会坐下时），情况就变了。学习者不再需要奖赏来区分正确和错误的反应。这时候，该转向间歇强化（intermittent reinforcement，也称为部分强化）了，即奖赏某些（而不是全部）正确反应。这种不那么频繁的强化程序——也许是每三次正确反应得到一次奖赏——仍然可以激励你的狗听从指挥，同时避免其获得过分满足。一般而言，无论我们是与人打交道还是与动物打交道，间歇强化都是维持已经学会的行为的最有效的方式（Robbins，1971；Terry，2000）。在实践中，将社会强化（“狗狗真棒！”）与更有形的奖赏（食物）相结合能有助于向间歇强化的过渡。
p40.en: Once the desired behavior takes place (for example, when your dog learns to sit down), the situation changes. Learners no longer need rewards to distinguish between right and wrong responses. It is time to turn to intermittent reinforcement, also known as partial reinforcement, which rewards some (and not all) correct reactions. This less frequent intensive procedure — perhaps a reward for the right response every three times — can still inspire your dog to follow command, while avoiding oversatisfaction. In general, intermittent reinforcement is the most effective way to sustain the behaviour that has been learned, whether we deal with people or with animals (Robbins, 1971); Terry, 2000. In practice, it strengthens society. This can be done in a more tangible way (food) to facilitate the transition to intermittent strengthening.

p41.original: 间歇强化的一大优势是它能抵抗消退，这意味着在间歇强化的帮助下发展起来的行为可能会持续更长时间。（操作性条件反射中的）消退会在强化停止时发生，就像赌徒放弃一直没有回报的老虎机一样。是什么让间歇强化如此抗消退？想象两个赌徒和两台老虎机。一台机器每次都会莫名其妙地吐钱出来，而另一台更正常的机器则以不可预测的间歇程序吐钱。现在，假设两台设备都突然停止吐钱。哪个赌徒会先发现？每次按下按钮都有收获（连续强化）的赌徒会很快注意到变化并停止赌博，而偶尔获胜（间歇强化）的赌徒可能会在没有奖赏的情况下继续赌很长时间，并寄希望于下一局能有所收获。
p41.en: One of the main advantages of intermittent reinforcement is its resistance to retreat, which means that behaviour developed with the help of intermittent reinforcement may last longer. Depression (in operational reflection) occurs at the end of the intensification, just as gamblers give up a tiger machine that has never been rewarded. What makes the intermittent reinforcement so resistant? Imagine two gamblers and two tiger machines. Each time, one machine spits out money in mysterious ways, while the other, more normal machine, throws up money in unpredictable intermittent procedures. Now, it is assumed that both devices suddenly stopped throwing up money. Which gambler will find out first? The gamblers who have a gain (continuously reinforced) in each case press the button quickly notice the change and stop gambling, while the gamblers who occasionally win (intermediately strengthened) may continue to gamble for a long time without a reward and hope that the next round will yield.

p43.original: 既然我们已经让你相信了间歇强化的威力，你应该知道它有两种主要形式，即两种强化程序（schedules of reinforcement）。
p43.en: Since we have convinced you of the power of intermittent reinforcement, you should know that it has two main forms, namely, two enhanced procedures.

p44.original: 1. 其中一种是比率强化程序（ratio schedule），在一定次数的反应后提供奖赏。
p44.en: 1. One of these is the ratio enhancement process (ratio scheme), which provides rewards after a certain number of reactions.

p45.original: 2. 另一种被称为间隔强化程序（interval schedule），在一定时间间隔后提供加强。
p45.en: 2. Another, known as the Interval Schedule, provides enhancements after a certain interval.

p46.original: 让我们看看每种强化程序的优缺点。
p46.en: Let us look at the strengths and weaknesses of each of the enhanced procedures.

p47.original: 比率强化程序 假设你拥有一家企业，并根据员工完成的工作量（例如，他们销售的每件商品）支付工资。在这种情况下你使用的就是比率强化程序。比率强化程序是指奖赏取决于正确反应的数量。心理学家进一步将比率强化程序区分为两种子类型，即固定比率和可变比率强化程序。当你在以下段落中读到它们时，请经常参考图4-5，它为每种强化类型都提供了一个直观摘要。
p47.en: The ratio enhancement procedure assumes that you own a business and pay salaries based on the work done by the employees (e.g., every commodity they sell). In this case, you're using the ratio enhancement program. The ratio enhancement procedure refers to the amount of reward that depends on the correct response. Psychologists further distinguish the ratio enhancement procedure between two subcategories, the fixed and variable ratio enhancement procedure. When you read them in the following paragraphs, please refer regularly to figures 4-5, which provide an intuitive summary of each type of reinforcement.

p49.original: 注：该图显示了由四种不同的强化程序产生的典型反应模式。（每条线上的短杠表示何时提供强化。）左上角那条线的陡峭角度显示了比率强化程序通常在一个时间段内如何比间隔强化程序带来更多的反应。
p49.en: Note: The figure shows typical response patterns resulting from four different enhanced procedures. (The short bars on each line indicate when reinforcement is provided. ) The steep angle of the upper left corner shows how the ratio enhancement program usually produces more reactions than the spacing enhancement program in a time period.

p50.original: 固定比率强化程序（fixed ratio schedules）在固定数量的反应后提供强化，无论多少，奖赏都是可以预测的。这种强化程序常常用于工业生产，例如，当工人按计件获得报酬时，即一定数量的生产对应一定数量的工资。因此，如果你拥有一家轮胎工厂，每生产5个轮胎就支付工人1美元，那么你使用的就是固定比率强化程序。在这种强化程序下，奖赏所需的工作量（反应数量）保持不变，但人们工作得越快，他们得到的钱就越多。也无怪乎管理层喜欢固定比率强化程序，因为反应率通常很高（Terry，2000；Whyte，1972）。换句话说，它可以让人们快速工作。零售店也使用固定比例的强化程序，例如，当你从当地某咖啡店购买10杯咖啡后获得一杯免费咖啡时，这会让你下一次回到同一家咖啡店喝咖啡。
p50.en: The fixed ratio enhancement process (fixed radio schedules) provides reinforcement after a fixed number of reactions, and rewards are predictable regardless of the amount. This intensification process is often used for industrial production, for example, when workers are paid individually, a certain amount of production corresponds to a certain amount of wages. So if you own a tyre factory and pay a worker $1 for every five tyres produced, then you use the fixed ratio enhancement procedure. Under this enhanced procedure, the amount of work required to reward (the number of reactions) remains the same, but the faster people work, the more money they receive. It is no wonder that management prefers the fixed ratio enhancement process, as the response rate is usually high (Terry, 2000); Whyte, 1972. In other words, it enables people to work quickly. Retail stores also use a fixed-rate intensive procedure, such as getting a free cup of coffee after you have purchased 10 coffees from a local coffee shop, which will allow you to return to the same coffee shop for coffee next time.

p51.original: 可变比率强化程序（variable ratio schedules）不太可预测，强化似乎是随机的。电话推销员的工作依据的是可变比率强化程序，因为他们永远不知道在达成下一笔买卖之前必须拨打多少次电话。视频扑克游戏中的玩家面对的也是可变比率强化程序，他们永远不知道机器何时会给出回报。在这两种情况下，强化对反应的要求不断变化，使得反应速率很高，以至于可变比率强化程序通常比任何其他强化程序都能带来更多的反应。在演示可变比率强化程序的强大威力时，斯金纳展示了一只饥饿的鸽子每小时会啄一个圆盘12 000次，以获得平均每啄110次才获得一次的奖赏（Skinner，1953）！因为鸽子永远不知道下一次啄食是否会带来食物，所以它不停地快速啄食来追逐奖赏。
p51.en: The variable ratio enhancement process (variable radio schedules) is not predictable and the reinforcement seems random. The work of the telephone promoters was based on the variable ratio enhancement process, as they never knew how many calls they had to make before the next sale was made. The video poker players are also facing a variable ratio enhancement program, and they never know when the machine will pay off. In both cases, the requirements for enhanced response have evolved to the point where the response rate is so high that the variable ratio enhancement process usually produces more responses than any other enhanced procedure. In demonstrating the power of the variable ratio enhancement process, Skinner showed a hungry pigeon pecking an hourly disk 12,000 times in order to get an average of 110 pecks to get a reward (Skinner, 1953)! Because the pigeon never knew whether the next peck would bring food, it kept pecking fast in pursuit of the reward.

p52.original: 间隔强化程序 时间是间隔强化程序的关键。换句话说，对于间隔强化程序，强化取决于特定时间段内的反应（而非反应次数，见图4-5）。与比率强化程序类似，心理学家也将间隔强化程序区分为两类：固定间隔和可变间隔强化程序。
p52.en: The interval enhancement program Time is the key to the interval enhancement program. In other words, for staggered procedures, enhancement depends on the response (rather than the number of responses) over a specific period of time (see figures 4-5). Similar to the ratio enhancement procedure, psychologists also distinguish between two types of staggered procedure: fixed and variable.

p53.original: 固定间隔强化程序（fixed interval schedules）在工作环境中常常出现，表现为定期薪水或上司在每月员工会议上的表扬。为每周测验而学习的学生也是根据固定时间间隔进行强化的。在所有这些情况下，时间间隔不会改变，因此奖赏之间的时间长度保持不变。你可能已发现，固定间隔强化一般会导致相对较低的反应率。具有讽刺意味的是，这是企业最广泛采用的强化程序。即使是在斯金纳箱中的大鼠，也很快就发现它只需要在一定间隔期间做有限的工作就能获得食物。比获得食物奖赏所需的次数更多地按下杠杆只是浪费能量。因此，固定间隔强化程序下的大鼠和人类可能一般只会显示微乎其微的产能，直到间隔接近结束时才快速增加反应率。（想想大学生们所面临的学期论文的截止日期，或者在考试前的死记硬背。）在图4-5中，你可以看到“扇形”的行为模式，这种行为模式是由每个间隔快结束时的一连串活动造成的。
p53.en: The fixed interval enhancements (fixed interval Schedules) are often found in the working environment, as reflected in regular pay or praise by supervisors at monthly staff meetings. Students studying for weekly tests are also reinforced on the basis of fixed time intervals. In all of these cases, the time interval will not change, so the length of time between rewards will remain unchanged. You may have found that a fixed interval reinforcement typically leads to a relatively low response rate. Ironically, this is the most widely used intensive procedure in enterprises. Even in the Skinner box, the rat quickly found that it needed only limited work at a certain time to obtain food. More leverage than is required for food rewards is simply a waste of energy. As a result, rats and humans under the Spacing Enhancement Program may generally only show minimal capacity and not increase their response rates until the interval closes to the end. (Think about the deadline for the semester papers that college students face, or the hard-on-the-script. In figures 4-5 you can see a pattern of “flank” behaviour, which is the result of a series of activities at the end of each interval.

p54.original: 可变间隔强化程序（variable interval schedules）可能是所有强化程序中最不可预测的。在可变间隔强化程序中，奖赏（或惩罚）之间的时间间隔并不是固定的。由此产生的反应率可能很高，但通常不如可变比率强化程序那么高。（你可以这样思考这个问题：你能在比率强化程序中控制奖赏的频率，因为你工作得越快，你就能越快达到奖赏所需的“魔法数”。但是，在间隔强化程序中，无论你工作快慢，你都不能让时间过得更快，因为你在指定的时间过去之前是不会收到奖赏的。）对于斯金纳箱中的一只鸽子或一只大鼠来说，可变间隔强化程序可能是这次等待30秒间隔，下次等待3分钟，再下次等待1分钟。课堂上的突击测验、老板的随机到访或工作中的药物测试都是可变间隔强化程序的例子。我们在等待电梯时可以观察到可变间隔强化程序的典型反应：因为每次按下呼叫按钮和电梯到达之间的延迟都不同，你的一些同伴就像斯金纳箱中的鸽子一样，会多次按下按钮，仿佛在不可预测的时间间隔内有更多的反应就能够控制电梯更快到达。
p54.en: The variable intervalent schedues is probably the least predictable of all enhancements. The time lag between rewards (or penalties) is not fixed in the context of the variable spacing enhancement process. The resulting response rate may be high, but it is generally less than the variable ratio enhancement process. (You can think of this: you can control the frequency of rewards in the ratio enhancement process, because the sooner you work, the sooner you can reach the “magic numbers” required for the rewards. However, in the stifling process, you cannot afford to pass time faster, regardless of how slow you are, because you will not receive a reward until the time specified has passed. For a pigeon or rat in the Skinner box, the variable spacing enhancement procedure may be the 30-second interval, the next three minutes and the next one-minute. School raids, random visits by the boss or drug tests at work are examples of variable-spacing enhancements. While we wait for the elevator, we can observe typical reactions to the variable-spacing enhancements: because each call button and the delay between the elevator arrival is different, some of your peers, like the pigeons in the Skinner box, press the button several times, as if more reactions were able to control the elevator's faster arrival within an unpredictable time interval.

p55.original: 4.4.5 生物基础在操作性条件反射中的作用
p55.en: 4.4.5 The role of the biological base in the reflection of operational conditions

p56.original: 食物可以强化饥饿的动物，水可以强化口渴的动物，我们从中容易看出，满足基本生物需求或欲望的刺激如何为生物体提供强化。类似地，对性唤起的生物体而言，发生性的机会成了强化物。心理学家将这些刺激称作初级强化物（primary reinforcer）。
p56.en: Food strengthens hungry animals, water strengthens thirsty animals, and it is easy to see how incentives to satisfy basic biological needs or desires can strengthen organisms. Similarly, the chances of sexual activity are reinforced for sexually induced organisms. Psychologists call these incentives primary reinforcements (primary reinforcer).

p57.original: 但是金钱或成绩提供的强化则不同：它们既不能吃，也不能喝，也不能直接满足任何生理需要。那么为什么这些东西会如此有力地强化行为？中性刺激，如金钱或等级，通过与初级强化物的关联而产生强化效果，因此其被称为操作性反应的条件强化物（conditioned reinforcer），又被称为次级强化物（secondary reinforcer）。赞美、认可的微笑、金色小星星、商人使用的“奖赏卡”以及各种身份象征也是如此。事实上，几乎任何刺激都可以通过与初级强化物建立关联而成为次级或条件性强化物。条件化足够强的时候，诸如金钱、地位或奖章等次级强化物本身甚至就可以成为终极目的。
p57.en: However, money or merit provide a different kind of reinforcement: they neither eat nor drink nor directly satisfy any biological needs. Then why are these things so powerfully reinforcing behavior? Moderate irritation, such as money or grade, has an enhanced effect by association with primary reinforcements and is therefore referred to as conditioned reinforcements for operational reaction (conditioned reinforcer) and as secondary reinforcer. The same applies to praises, acknowledged smiles, golden stars, “reward cards” used by businessmen, and various identity symbols. In fact, almost any stimulus can become a secondary or conditional reinforcement by establishing links to primary reinforcements. When conditions are strong enough, sub-strengths such as money, status or medals can become even the ultimate end in themselves.

p58.original: 初级和次级强化物之间的区别提示我们一个更微妙之处：像经典条件反射一样，操作性条件反射不仅仅是学习，而是存在相应的生物学根源——因而我们对某些强化物有着“内嵌”偏好（“垃圾”食品的制造商用高糖高脂食品投我们所好）。
p58.en: The distinction between primary and secondary reinforcements points to a more subtle point: like classic retroreflection, the operational refraction is not just a study, but a corresponding biological source — so we have an “embedded” preference for certain fortifications (the manufacturers of “spam” foods put on us high sugar and fat).

p59.original: 这里有另一个例子，显示了操作性条件反射中生物基础的威力。我们来讲讲凯勒·布雷兰兹（Keller Breland）和马利安·布雷兰兹（Marian Breland）的故事，他们是斯金纳的两名学生，从事动物训练业务，但在训练猪时他们曾遇到一些出乎意料的麻烦。你或许了解，猪是一种聪明的动物。因此，布雷兰兹夫妇可以毫不费力地教导它们捡起圆形的木制代币并将之存入“存钱罐”。问题是，在几周内，这些猪恢复了猪的行为：它们会反复丢下代币，用嘴拱，铲向空中，然后再用嘴拱。这发生在经过训练的猪身上。为什么如此？因为用嘴拱是猪的本能行为。布雷兰兹夫妇（Breland & Breland，1961）在浣熊、鸡、鲸鱼和奶牛等多种生物中发现了类似的模式，并创造了本能漂移（instinct drift）一词来描述这种先天反应倾向对学习行为的干扰。因此，无怪乎人们无法让他们的猫停止抓挠家具，或者无法完全避免垃圾食品对自身的诱惑。
p59.en: Here is another example of the power of the operational conditions reflecting the biological base. Let's talk about Keller Breland and Marian Breland, two students from Skinner who were in the animal training business, but who had some unexpected problems in training pigs. You might understand that pigs are a smart animal. Thus, the Brauzs could, without any effort, teach them to pick up round wooden coins and deposit them in “cans”. The problem is that in a few weeks, the pigs reverted to their actions: they would repeatedly drop their coins, use their mouths, shovel them into the air and then use their mouths. This happened to trained pigs. Why? Because mouth arches are the instinct of pigs. Mr. and Mrs. Breland (Breland & Breland, 1961) found similar patterns in a variety of organisms, such as raccoons, chickens, whales and cows, and created the word instinct drifting to describe this congenital reactionary tendency to interfere with learning behaviour. It is therefore no wonder that people cannot stop their cats from scratching furniture or completely avoid the temptation of junk foods to themselves.

p61.original: 令人欣慰的是，相比猪，心理学家更成功地将代币用于人类。代币经济系统是一种为所需行为提供代币的强化类型；当赢取的代币足够多时，人们可以用其兑换各种奖赏或特权。代币可以是筹码、弹珠、贴纸、邮票、假的钱、积分、复选标记或任何其他易于实施和跟踪的事物。
p61.en: It is gratifying to note that psychologists have been more successful in using tokens for humans than pigs. The currency economy system is a form of reinforcement to provide the required act; When there are enough coins to win, people can exchange them for various rewards or privileges. The token may be chips, marbles, stickers, stamps, counterfeit money, credits, recheck marks or any other thing that is easy to implement and track.

p62.original: 教师已经成功地将代币经济用于从学龄前到大学阶段的学生身上。在幼儿中，基于标记的策略，如贴纸图表和笑脸贴纸能够促使学生快速完成任务，即当老师发现学生做得好时，学生会得到一颗星星或笑脸贴纸。学生可以在之后将他们的贴纸（或任何代币）换成零食或其他想要的物品（Doll et al.，2013）。在小学，代币的使用提高了作业的完成率——每次学生完成一项作业，他们都会获得一个代币，几个代币就可以交换自由时间（Ruesch & McLaughlin，1981）。如果与不当行为的“成本”（失去已获得的代币）相结合，结果甚至更好。一项针对很少完成作业的中学生的研究发现，采用为工作表上的每个答案记1～2分的代币系统（获得足够的分数后可以换取课堂上使用计算机的时间），作业的完成率可以从34%提高到79%（Flaman & McLaughlin，1986）！而在大学生中，学生由于提出好问题而获得的代金券（可在课堂上兑换额外分数）显著提高了课堂讨论的参与度（Nelson，2010）。
p62.en: Teachers have been successful in using the currency economy for students from the preschool to the university level. In young children, tag-based strategies, such as stickers and smile-face stickers, enable students to perform their tasks quickly, i.e. when teachers find that they do well, they get a star or smile-face sticker. Students can then exchange their stickers (or any currency) for snacks or other desired items (Doll et al., 2013). In primary schools, the use of tokens increases the completion rate - each time a student completes a job, they receive a token, and several coins can exchange free time (Ruesch & McLaughlin, 1981). If combined with the “cost” of misconduct (loss of acquired coins), the result is even better. A study of secondary school students who rarely completed their work found that the completion rate could be increased from 34 per cent to 79 per cent by introducing a token system of between one and two points for each answer on the worksheet (to obtain sufficient points in exchange for time to use computers in the classroom) (Flaman & McLaughlin, 1986). In the case of university students, the voucher (which allows for the exchange of extra points in class) obtained by students for good questions has significantly increased the level of participation in classroom discussions (Nelson, 2010).

p63.original: 代币经济适用于所有年龄段。想想你可以如何将这个概念应用于你自己的目标。
p63.en: The currency economy applies to all age groups. Think about how you can apply this concept to your own goals.

p64.original: 代币经济在家庭和社区环境中也很有效。在家里，父母可以使用代币经济系统来激励他们的孩子完成家庭作业、做家务和进行社会期许的行为（Doll et al.，2013）。精神卫生机构和康复之家已经在利用条件强化物的力量来激励患者做出适宜的、有益健康的行为（Ayllon & Azrin，1965；Holden，1978）。与其他形式的治疗相结合，代币经济可以帮助患者学习如何在真实的世界中有效行事的策略（Kazdin，1994）。最近，代币经济在治疗孤独症方面也很有成效（Matson & Boisjoli，2009）。
p64.en: The currency economy is also effective in family and community settings. In the home, parents can use the currency economic system to motivate their children to perform their homework, housework and socially expected behaviour (Doll et al., 2013). Mental health institutions and rehabilitation homes already use the strength of condition-enhanced devices to motivate patients to behave appropriately and healthyly (Ayllon & Azrin, 1965); Holden, 1978. In combination with other forms of treatment, the currency economy can help patients learn strategies to act effectively in the real world (Kazdin, 1994). Recently, the currency economy has also been effective in treating autism (Matson & Boisjoli, 2009).

p65.original: 代币经济的一个主要优势是它们能够兼顾即时奖赏和长期奖赏。因此，它们在促进长期行为改变方面特别有效。要用操作性条件化来改变某些行为（例如，吃更健康的饮食），挑战之一是我们必须首先抵制即时满足的诱惑（例如，多汁的汉堡），而即时的诱惑的力量远超获得遥不可及的未来奖赏（例如，减肥或皮肤更清爽）的吸引力。代币经济有助于弥合这一差距。例如，如果你想吃得更健康，请尝试在每次成功地克服吃不健康食物的冲动时给自己一些代币，在你赚取了一些代币后，你可以将它们换成你想要的东西（也许是和朋友喝咖啡或看电影、你一直想买的新东西或任何可能激励你的东西）。为自己提供多样化的奖赏也是有帮助的，这样你就不会因为对某一种奖赏感到过分满足而失去动力。根据这些原则，你可以如何使用代币经济来帮助自己实现某种行为目标呢，例如，让学习更持之以恒或定期锻炼？
p65.en: One of the main advantages of the currency economy is that they combine instant and long-term rewards. They are therefore particularly effective in promoting long-term behavioural change. One of the challenges in changing behaviour by operationalizing conditions (e.g., eating a healthier diet) is that we must first resist the temptation of instant satisfaction (e.g., juicy burgers), which is far more than the attraction to a distant reward for the future (e.g., loss of weight or better skin). The currency economy helps to bridge this gap. For example, if you want to eat healthier, try to give yourself some tokens every time you succeed in overcoming the urge to eat unhealthy food, and after you earn some tokens, you can exchange them for what you want (perhaps drinking coffee with friends or watching movies, new things you've always wanted to buy, or anything that might inspire you). It would also be helpful to offer yourself a diverse reward, so that you do not lose momentum because you are oversatisfied with a reward of one kind. Under these principles, how can you use the currency economy to help you achieve a certain behavioural goal, for example, by making learning more constant or by exercising regularly?

p66.original: 4.4.7 借助喜好的活动作为强化物：普雷马克原则
p66.en: 4.4.7 Use of preferred activities as reinforcements: the Premak principle

p67.original: 另一种强化行为的方法是利用个体喜欢做的活动（即对个体来说有趣的活动）作为其完成不太想做的任务的奖赏。例如，经常锻炼的人可能会使用每天的跑步或健身课作为完成其他不太愉快的任务的奖赏。同样，教师们发现，如果用稍后跑动和制造噪声的机会作为强化（Homme et al.，1963），可以让幼儿学会静坐不动（Homme et al.，1963）。心理学家以其发现者命名，称之为普雷马克原则（Premack principle）。戴维·普雷马克（Premack，1965）最先在口渴的大鼠身上展示了这个概念，如果在锻炼之后获得喝水的机会，那么这些大鼠就会花更多的时间在锻炼轮上跑动。相反，另一组被剥夺运动但不口渴的大鼠，如果在喝水之后可以获得在锻炼轮上跑动的机会，那么它们就会学会喝更多的水。父母可以用完全相同的方式使用普雷马克原则让孩子整理床铺或洗碗，即在孩子完成任务之后给予其与朋友一起玩的机会。
p67.en: Another way to strengthen behaviour is to use the activities that individuals like to do (i.e., those that are interesting to individuals) as rewards for the tasks they do not want to do. For example, people who exercise regularly may use daily running or fitness classes as rewards for other less pleasant tasks. Similarly, teachers found that the early childhood learning system could be held still if the opportunity to run and make noise at a later stage was used as a boost (Homme et al., 1963). The psychologist is named Premack principle, after his founder. Premack, 1965, first demonstrated this concept in thirsty rats, who would spend more time running on the exercise wheel if they were given the opportunity to drink water after exercise. Conversely, another group of distraught but thirsty rats learn to drink more if they have the opportunity to run on a exercise wheel after drinking water. Parents can use the Premak principle in exactly the same way as children to prepare their beds or to wash dishes, i.e. to give them the opportunity to play with their friends after they have completed their mission.

p69.original: 操作性学习法则适用于所有拥有大脑的生物。强化背后的生物学机制在不同物种之间似乎是相同的。究竟什么可以作为强化物，在不同物种之间差别很大。我们对于初级强化物的了解是，食物可以强化饥饿生物的行为，水可以强化口渴生物的行为，因为二者满足了与生存相关的基本需求。但是，某个特定的个体满足基本需求的方式可能既取决于生存本能，也可能取决于学习，尤其是对于人类而言，次级强化是非常重要的。在决定什么将成为我们的强化物方面，文化发挥着尤为强大的作用。因此，虽然某些文化中的人会觉得吃蟋蟀是一种强化，但欧美地区的大多数人却不会。同样，某些教会的教徒会觉得清除吵闹的蟋蟀既明智又有益，但佛教徒却厌恶这种做法。类似地，请注意，观看一场板球比赛可能对英国板球迷是一种奖赏，但是对大多数美国人来说却乏味至极。
p69.en: Operational learning applies to all organisms with a brain. The biological mechanisms behind the strengthening seem to be the same among different species. What can be used as a reinforcement varies considerably between species. Our understanding of primary fortifications is that food can reinforce the behaviour of hungry organisms, and water can reinforce the behaviour of thirsty organisms, as they meet the basic needs associated with survival. However, the way in which a particular individual meets basic needs may depend on both survival instincts and learning, especially for human beings, where secondary reinforcement is important. Culture plays a particularly powerful role in determining what will become our strength. Thus, while some cultures may feel that eating cricket is an enhancement, most people in Europe and the United States do not. Similarly, certain church members would find it wise and useful to remove noisy crickets, but Buddhists would hate it. Similarly, note that watching a cricket game may be a reward for British cricket fans, but it is boring for most Americans.

p70.original: 某些文化的人群嗜好把昆虫作为一种食物，对于这些人来说，吃昆虫是一种强化。
p70.en: For people of certain cultures who prefer insects as food, eating them is an intensification.

p71.original: 因此，文化塑造了人们对强化物的不同偏好，而强化物也塑造了文化。当你第一次走在陌生城市的街道上时，所有吸引你眼球的差异都只是人们找到的获得强化或逃避惩罚的不同方式。寺庙容纳了从神那里寻求奖赏的文化尝试。衣着或许反映了寻求好伴侣或舒适感的一些尝试。一种文化下的饮食习惯是从学习依靠本地植物和动物资源生存的过程中演变而来的。从这个意义上说，文化是最初由操作性条件反射而被习得，并且在一群人之中共有的一组行为。
p71.en: Culture thus shapes different preferences for reinforcements, which also shape culture. When you first walk on the streets of strange cities, all the differences that attract your eyes are just different ways of being reinforced or escaping punishment. The temples accommodate cultural attempts to seek rewards from God. Clothes may reflect some attempts to find a good partner or comfort. A cultural diet has evolved from learning to survive on native plants and animal resources. In this sense, culture is a group of behaviours that were first learned from operational reflections and shared among a group of people.

p74.original: 评估使用惩罚塑造行为的相关争议。
p74.en: Assessing disputes related to the use of penalties to shape behaviour.

p75.original: 正如学校教师和监狱看守所证明的那样，将惩罚作为影响行为的手段会造成一些困难。在理想情况下，我们可能会认为惩罚是强化的对立面，是一种用于削弱令人厌恶的后果的行为。与强化类似，惩罚有两种主要形式。
p75.en: As demonstrated by school teachers and prison facilities, the use of punishment as a means of influencing behaviour poses some difficulties. Ideally, we might consider punishment to be a reinforced opposite and an act designed to weaken the repugnant consequences. Similar to strengthening, there are two main forms of punishment.

p76.original: 1. 正惩罚需要施加厌恶刺激，就像当你触碰一个滚烫的碟子之后，痛苦的后果会降低你重复这种行为的可能。
p76.en: 1. The punishment requires the imposition of an aversion stimulus, as if the painful consequences reduce the possibility of repeating such acts when you touch a hot plate.

p77.original: 2. 另一种主要的惩罚形式——负惩罚，则是去除强化物，就像父母拿走行为不端的青少年的车钥匙一样。
p77.en: Another major form of punishment — the punishment — is the removal of the reinforcements, just as parents take the car keys of the misdemeanor young person.

p78.original: （你会发现，当应用于惩罚时，正惩罚和负惩罚发挥作用的方式与被应用于强化时相同：正惩罚添加一些东西，而负惩罚移除一些东西。）然而，从技术上讲，这是惩罚所存在的问题之一，即厌恶刺激只有在实际上削弱了造成它出现的行为时才起到了惩罚的作用。从这个意义上说，打屁股或超速罚单是不是惩罚，要取决于结果。
p78.en: (You will find that when punishment is applied, the punishment and the punishment work in the same way as when it is reinforced: the punishment adds something and the punishment removes something. Technically, however, this is one of the problems with punishment, namely, that aversion is only punitive when it actually weakens the behaviour that caused it to occur. In this sense, ass-beating or speeding tickets are not punishable, depending on the outcome.

p80.original: 你可能已经注意到，惩罚和负强化都涉及令人不快的刺激。你如何区分这两者？让我们从以下示例来看看惩罚与负强化有何不同（见图4-6）。
p80.en: You may have noticed that both punishment and negative reinforcement involve unpleasant incentives. How do you distinguish between the two? Let us look at the following examples of how penalties differ from negative reinforcements (see figures 4-6).

p81.original: 图4-6 负强化与惩罚对比

p82.original: 惩罚会减少行为或降低其再次发生的可能性。相比之下，负强化就像正强化一样，总是增加反应再次发生的可能性。同时，不要忘记正和负这两个修饰语意味着“添加”和“移除”；作为操作性条件反射中的修饰语，它们与“好”和“坏”无关。因此，正强化和正惩罚都涉及给予或“添加”刺激。另外，负强化和负惩罚总是涉及抑制或消除刺激。
p82.en: Punishment reduces behaviour or reduces the likelihood of its recurrence. By contrast, negative reinforcement, as it is being strengthened, always increases the likelihood that reactions will recur. At the same time, do not forget that the two qualifiers, positive and negative, mean “add” and “removal”; As qualifiers in the reflection of operational conditions, they have nothing to do with “good” and “bad”. Thus, both the enhanced and the positive penalties are related to the granting or “adding” of incentives. In addition, both aggravated and punitive are always related to inhibiting or eliminating incentives.

p83.original: 还有最后一点需要记住：我们经常可以预测特定的后果会对未来的行为产生什么样的影响，但确定它是强化物还是惩罚物的唯一方法是观察它对行为的影响。例如，虽然我们可能会猜测打屁股对孩子是一种惩罚，但与之相伴的对孩子的关注却可能恰恰强化了我们不希望孩子做出的行为。
p83.en: There is also a final point to remember: we can often predict the impact of particular consequences on future behaviour, but the only way to determine whether it is a reinforcement or a punishment is to observe its effects on conduct. For example, while we may speculate that spanking is a punishment for a child, the accompanying attention to the child may only reinforce the behaviour we do not want the child to do.

p84.original: 对正负强化与正负惩罚之间区别的简要总结参见表4-1。
p84.en: A brief summary of the distinction between positive and negative reinforcement and positive and negative punishment is given in Table 4-1.

p87.original: 举一个你自己生活中的负强化影响行为的例子并解释你的回答。
p87.en: Take an example of negative-effecting behaviour in your own life and explain your answer.

p90.original: 许多社会制度严重依赖惩罚，威胁人们要实施惩罚来使其“循规蹈矩”。例如，对人们罚款，打小孩屁股，给学生差的成绩，开停车罚单，以及露出不赞成的表情。在世界各地和整个历史上，各种文化都惯常采用社交隔离、石刑（用乱石砸死）、鞭打、监禁以及各种堪称创造性的惩罚方法，以试图阻止不可接受的行为。目前，美国拘留所和监狱约有150万人，而美国目前每35名公民中就有一人在拘留所或监狱，或是处于缓刑或假释中（Glaze & Kaeble，2014）。（信不信由你，这些数字近年来已有所下降。）
p90.en: Many social systems rely heavily on punishment, threatening to impose punishment to make them “business as usual”. For example, fines were imposed on people, ass-beating children, bad grades for students, parking tickets and expressions of disapproval. Throughout the world and throughout history, social segregation, stoning (by stoning), flogging, imprisonment and various creative methods of punishment have been routinely used by cultures to try to stop unacceptable behaviour. There are currently approximately 1.5 million people in United States detention facilities and prisons, and one in 35 citizens in the United States is currently in detention or prison or on probation or parole (Glaze & Kaeble, 2014). (Believe you, these figures have declined in recent years. I don't think so.

p91.original: 为什么我们如此频繁地使用惩罚？一方面，它有时会促使行为立即发生变化。另一方面，惩罚者可能会通过实施惩罚而感到满足，他们会感觉自己“算了账”，他们会“扯平了”，或让对方“付出了代价”。这就是为什么我们有时会用“甜蜜的”来描述复仇，这种感情潜藏于公众对惩罚违法者的态度之中（Carlsmith，2006）。
p91.en: Why do we use punishment so often? On the one hand, it sometimes leads to immediate changes in behaviour. On the other hand, the punishmenter may feel satisfied by the imposition of the penalty, and they will feel that they “gone”, they will “bail even” or they will “pay the price”. That is why we sometimes describe revenge as “sweet”, a feeling embedded in public attitudes to punish violators (Carlsmith, 2006).

p92.original: 但惩罚——尤其是那种涉及痛苦、羞辱或监禁的惩罚——从长远来看通常效果不佳（American Psychological Association，2002）。受惩罚的儿童可能会继续行为不端，受训斥的员工可能会蓄意破坏生产目标的实现。尽管有各种严厉的惩罚手段，世界各地仍有人在犯罪。那么，为什么惩罚如此难以奏效呢？有几个原因。
p92.en: However, punishment — especially those involving pain, humiliation or imprisonment — is usually ineffective in the long run (American Psychological Association, 2002). The child may continue to be punished for misconduct and the trained staff may deliberately undermine the achievement of the goal of production. Despite severe punishments, crime continues to be committed in various parts of the world. Why, then, is the punishment so ineffectual? There are several reasons.

p94.original: 1. 惩罚与强化不同，必须持续执行。当知道高速公路巡逻队在监视时，司机会遵守限速规则；当父母在附近时，安德烈不会打他的弟弟；当劫匪用枪指着你时，你可能会交出你的钱包。但是当惩罚的威胁被移除时，惩罚抑制行为的力量通常就会消失（Skinner，1953）。如果惩罚不太可能发生，它就起不到威慑作用；而在大多数情况下，惩罚不可能得到持续执行。间歇性惩罚远不如每次都在不良行为出现后就实施惩罚有效。事实上，不惩罚不良行为会起到奖赏的效果，比如，主管忽视员工迟到这件事。一般而言，只有当你始终可以控制环境（从而管理惩罚）时，你才能通过惩罚或威胁来控制某人的行为，但是完全控制几乎不可行。
p94.en: 1. The punishment must be imposed on a continuous basis, unlike the strengthening. When it is known that the highway patrol is watching, the division has the opportunity to observe the speed limit; Andre will not beat his brother when his parents are near; When the robber points a gun at you, you might hand over your wallet. But when the threat of punishment is removed, the power to punish inhibition usually disappears (Skinner, 1953). If punishment is unlikely to occur, it will not serve as a deterrent; In most cases, however, the punishment cannot be sustained. Interruptive punishment is far less effective than the imposition of punishment every time a misdemeanour occurs. In fact, failure to punish misconduct can have the effect of rewarding, for example, by neglecting the lateness of employees. Generally speaking, you can control someone's behaviour by punishment or threat only if you can always control the environment (and thus manage the punishment), but complete control is almost impossible.

p95.original: 2. 即使可能会有惩罚，但奖赏的诱惑仍会让人为此付出代价。这可能是影响毒品交易的一个因素，即赚大钱的可能性超过坐牢的可能性（Levitt & Dubner，2005）。惩罚和奖赏也会以一种稍有不同的方式共同影响节食者：食物所带来的即时满足感可能会压倒吃了之后体重增加造成的不良后果。因此，当你试图通过惩罚来控制某人的行为时，如果你没有消除奖赏，你可能就会失败。
p95.en: 2. Even if there may be punishment, the temptation to reward can still be costly. This may be a factor influencing the drug trade, i.e. the likelihood of making a large sum of money is greater than the likelihood of prison (Levitt & Dubner, 2005). Penalties and rewards also affect dieters in a slightly different way: the immediate satisfaction of food may outweigh the adverse consequences of weight gain after eating. So when you try to control someone's behavior through punishment, if you don't eliminate the reward, you may fail.

p96.original: 3. 惩罚引发逃避或攻击。当受到惩罚时，生物体的生存本能会使它逃避惩罚，或以其他方式避免进一步的惩罚。如果逃跑被阻止，会导致生物体的攻击行为。将受伤的动物逼到角落，它可能会野蛮地攻击你。把两只大鼠放在一个地板网格带电的斯金纳箱里，大鼠会互相攻击（Ulrich & Azrin，1962）。将人类置于严酷的监狱环境中，他们可能会制造骚乱或做出其他攻击行为；狱警则可能虐待囚犯（Zimbardo，2004b，2007）。
p96.en: 3. Punishment triggers evasion or attack. When punished, the survival instinct of the organism would allow it to escape punishment or otherwise avoid further punishment. If flight is prevented, this could lead to attacks by organisms. Push the wounded animal into the corner and it could savagely attack you. Two rats were placed in a Skinner box with electric power in a floor grid, and rats attacked each other (Ulrich & Azrin, 1962). (b) Placing human beings in harsh prison conditions, which may cause disturbances or other attacks; Prison guards may ill-treat prisoners (Zimbardo, 2004b, 2007).

p97.original: 4. 在认同惩罚的环境中，无论是监狱、学校、工作场所还是家庭，人们会学会将惩罚和攻击作为影响他人的合理手段。惩罚与攻击性的联系也解释了为什么虐待孩子的父母通常在儿时遭受过虐待，以及为什么攻击性犯罪者一般来自对攻击性行为司空见惯的家庭（Golden，2000）。不幸的是，公众对惩罚与攻击性之间的这种证据确凿的关系仍然知之甚少。
p97.en: 4. In an environment where punishment is accepted, whether in prisons, schools, workplaces or families, people learn to use punishment and assault as a reasonable means of influencing others. The link between punishment and aggressiveness also explains why parents who abuse children are often abused as children, and why aggressors generally come from families where aggressive behaviour is common (Golden, 2000). Unfortunately, there is still little public awareness of this proven relationship between punishment and aggression.

p98.original: 5. 惩罚常常无效的第五个原因是，惩罚会使学习者感觉恐惧或忧虑，从而阻碍了对新的和更理想的反应的学习。由于无法逃脱惩罚，生物体最终可能会放弃逃跑或战斗的尝试，而屈从于压倒性的绝望感。这种对被惩罚的宿命的被动接受带来了一种被称为习得性无助的行为模式（Overmier & Seligman，1967）。对于人类而言，这种反应会导致被称为抑郁症的精神障碍（Terry，2000）。如果你想建设性地改变态度和行为，习得性无助和抑郁绝不是你希望得到的，攻击和逃避也绝不是。相比之下，没有受到惩罚的个体更愿意尝试新的行为。
p98.en: 5. A fifth reason why punishment is often ineffective is that it can create fear or anxiety among learners, thus hindering learning about new and more desirable responses. Without impunity, organisms may eventually give up attempts to flee or fight and succumb to overwhelming despair. This passive acceptance of punished destiny has brought about a pattern of behaviour known as acquired helplessness (Overmier & Seligman, 1967). For humans, this reaction can lead to mental disorders known as depression (Terry, 2000). If you want to change attitudes and behaviour constructively, it is not what you want to learn, it is not what you want to attack and avoid. By contrast, individuals who have not been punished are more willing to try new behaviour.

p99.original: 6. 然而，惩罚措施可能失败的第六个原因是，惩罚在实施时自带不公平性，经常违反我们的公平和平等的标准。例如，父母和老师惩罚男孩的次数多于女孩（Lytton & Romney，1991）。儿童（尤其是小学生）受到的体罚也比成年人多。再举一个例子，我们的学校乃至整个社会惩罚少数群体成员的次数比惩罚多数群体成员的频率更高（Hyman，1996）。
p99.en: 6. However, the sixth reason for the possible failure of punitive measures is that they are applied in an unfair manner, often in violation of our standards of fairness and equality. For example, parents and teachers punish boys more often than girls (Lytton & Romney, 1991). Children, especially primary school students, are also more physically punished than adults. To take another example, the punishment of members of minority groups is more frequent in our schools and in society at large than in the majority (Hyman, 1996).

p100.original: 7. 也许最重要的是，惩罚没有教会学习者应该做什么，因为它把注意力集中在了不做什么上。它顶多能做到制止不可取的行为，却没有提示什么是替代的、更可取的行为。
p100.en: 7. Perhaps most importantly, the punishment of those who do not learn from the Church should be done because it focuses on what they do not do. At best, it can stop undesirable behaviour without suggesting anything that is alternative and preferable.

p101.original: 高度惩罚性的环境可能会导致监狱骚乱和其他的攻击行为。
p101.en: A highly punitive environment may lead to prison disturbances and other attacks.

p103.original: 在某些限定的情况下，惩罚的效果非常好。例如，有的孤独症儿童可能会通过撞击头部或咬掉手指上的肉来严重伤害自己，此时惩罚可以阻止他们这种自我毁灭的行为。轻微的电击或往脸上泼冰水可以迅速阻止这些不良行为，尽管效果可能是暂时的（Holmes，2001）。惩罚也可以与强化有效地结合起来——就像学生因（努力）学习而获得了好成绩，不学习则不及格一样。如果你的小狗在咬你最喜欢的鞋子，你可以将惩罚与强化结合起来，拿走鞋子并说“不”，同时立即用可接受的咀嚼玩具替代鞋子，并在小狗咬玩具时表扬它。
p103.en: In certain limited cases, the punishment has been very effective. For example, some autistic children may seriously harm themselves by hitting their heads or biting off the meat on their fingers, when punishment can prevent them from doing this act of self-destruction. Light electric shocks or ice-creaming on the face can quickly deter these abuses, although the effects may be temporary (Homes, 2001). Punishment can also be combined with reinforcement - just as students achieve good results through (deployed) learning, and fail to do so. If your dog is biting your favorite shoe, you can combine punishment with reinforcement, take the shoes and say "no" and immediately replace them with acceptable chewing toys and praise them when they bite.

p104.original: 如果惩罚的后果合乎逻辑，那么它也更有可能成功。合乎逻辑的后果指的是与不良行为密切相关的后果，而不是与不良行为无关的惩罚，像打屁股或禁足。因此，如果孩子将玩具卡车留在了楼梯上，合乎逻辑的后果可能是丢失玩具一周。再举一个例子，晚回家吃晚饭的合乎逻辑的后果是吃冷饭。
p104.en: If the consequences of punishment are logical, it is also more likely to succeed. Logically, the consequences are those closely related to the misconduct, not those that are unrelated to the misconduct, such as spanking or grounded. Therefore, if a child leaves a toy truck on the stairs, the logical consequence may be a week of lost toys. To give another example, the logical consequence of coming home late for dinner is cold meals.

p105.original: 研究支持将逻辑后果、消退和对理想替代反应的奖赏相结合，而不是单纯对不良行为进行惩罚。使用惩罚的前提应该是满足以下条件。
p105.en: Research supports a combination of logical consequences, abdication and rewards for desirable alternatives, rather than simply punishing misconduct. The use of penalties should be subject to the following conditions.

p106.original: 惩罚应该一以贯之，每当不受欢迎的行为发生时都要进行惩罚。当不良行为未被惩罚时，实际相当于实施不良行为者获得了奖赏，从而使其行为更难改变。
p106.en: The punishment should be consistent and be applied whenever undesirable acts occur. When misconduct is not punished, the actual equivalent of a reward for its commission makes it more difficult to change its behaviour.

p107.original: 惩罚应该迅速，即立即进行。任何拖延都会削弱其有效性，因而“等你爸爸回家打你屁股”是一种糟糕的惩罚策略。
p107.en: The punishment should be carried out promptly and immediately. Any delay would diminish its effectiveness, so "when your father comes home and beats you up" was a bad punishment strategy.

p108.original: 惩罚的持续时间和强度应该是有限的，足以阻止相应行为即可，以“使惩罚力度与犯罪程度相称”。
p108.en: The duration and intensity of the punishment should be limited enough to deter the corresponding conduct, “to match the severity of the punishment to the degree of the crime”.

p109.original: 惩罚应明确针对相应行为，并且是行为的逻辑后果，而不是人身攻击（羞辱、讽刺或辱骂）或身体疼痛。
p109.en: The punishment should be clearly directed at the corresponding act and be the logical consequence of the act, not physical assault (stigmatizing, sarcasm or verbal abuse) or physical pain.

p110.original: 惩罚应仅限于相应的行为反应已经发生的情况下。
p110.en: The penalty shall be limited to the case where the corresponding behavioural reaction has occurred.

p111.original: 惩罚不应向被惩罚者传达混杂的信息（例如，“你不能打别人，但我可以打你”）。
p111.en: The punishment shall not convey a mixed message to the punished (e.g. “You can't hit others, but I can hit you”).

p112.original: 最有效的惩罚通常是负惩罚，例如，丧失特权；而不是施加令人不快的刺激，例如，打屁股。
p112.en: The most effective punishment is usually punitive, e.g. loss of privileges; Instead of imposing unpleasant irritation, for example, spanking.

p113.original: 4.6 改变操作性行为的检查清单
p113.en: 4.6 Checklist for Change in Operational Behaviour

p115.original: 将操作性条件反射应用于现实生活中的问题。
p115.en: Application of operational conditions reflection to real-life problems.

p116.original: 想一想你希望改变其行为的人。举例而言，让我们假设你的侄女玛蒂似乎越发暴躁，甚至当你带她去公共场合时也是如此。操作性条件反射提供了一系列可以提供帮助的工具：各种程序的正强化，加上负强化、消退和惩罚。
p116.en: Think of someone you want to change their behavior. Let's assume, for example, that your niece, Marty, seems to be getting more angry, even when you take her to a public place. Operational reflections provide a range of tools that can help: positive reinforcement of procedures, plus negative reinforcement, retortment and punishment.

p117.original: 既然正强化一直是不错的选择，请确定并鼓励可取的行为来代替不受欢迎的行为。最高效的父母和老师通常会将孩子的注意力转移到其他一些强化活动上来做到这一点。例如，当你带她去百货店时，你可以让她在绿苹果或红苹果之间做出简单的选择，这会让她对逛百货店本身保持兴趣，有助于防止她发脾气，也让你有机会为她的帮助提供积极的强化。（“好主意，玛蒂——我也喜欢红色的！”）并且，不要忽视普雷马克原则，如果玛蒂在一段时间内表现得很好，就让她做一些她喜欢做的事。（顺便说一句，这就是塑造发挥作用的地方：若要行之有效，你必须为玛蒂设定她能达到的目标，这样她才能实现这些目标并从正强化中获益。所以，你最初的目标可能是20分钟的良好行为，然后在她实现目标得到奖赏后，逐渐设定越来越长的时间。）首先使用连续强化，然后伴以间歇强化程序，以保证她不发脾气。
p117.en: Since strengthening has always been a good option, please identify and encourage desirable behaviour as a substitute for unwelcome behaviour. The most efficient parents and teachers usually turn their children's attention to other intensive activities. For example, when you take her to the department store, you can let her make a simple choice between the green apples and the red apples, which keeps her interested in going to the department store itself, helps to prevent her from getting angry and gives you the opportunity to actively strengthen her help. "Good idea, Maddie. I like red too. Moreover, the Premak principle should not be ignored, and if Maddie had performed well over time, she would have done something she liked to do. (Incidentally, this is where the shaping works: if you are to be effective, you have to set what Matty can achieve so that she can achieve those goals and benefit from being strengthened. So, your initial target may be 20 minutes of good behavior, and then gradually, after she's been rewarded for her goals, it's going to take longer and longer. (a) To use continuous reinforcements, followed by intermittent reinforcements, to ensure that she does not lose her temper.

p118.original: 负强化也有用。例如，如果玛蒂的一项家务是倒垃圾，你可以告诉她，如果她那天下午与她妹妹玩耍时能和谐相处（没有发脾气），你就会帮她倒垃圾。这样，通过让她避免一些她不愿做的事情（倒垃圾），我们强化了她的良好行为。你自己可能也享受过负强化，例如，某位教授允许你在平日考试成绩足够高时不用参加期末考试；或者允许你在课堂上实现了其他一些重要目标时不用做家庭作业。然而，负强化的应用效果较差。例如，父母通常会用唠叨来试图让他们的孩子打扫房间。在这种情况下，孩子会为了避免被唠叨而被迫打扫房间。虽然这可能会有效果，但是通常并不令人愉快。相反，行为主义者会建议父母创造积极的强化物来激励孩子打扫房间。通过提供有意义的奖赏、使用代币经济或使用普雷马克原则来鼓励期望的行为，你同样可以改变行为，而不会遭受伴随唠叨或其他厌恶刺激而带来的紧张气氛。
p118.en: Negative reinforcement is also useful. For example, if one of Maddie's chores was garbage disposal, you could tell her that if she had a good time with her sister that afternoon (without a temper), you would have helped her with garbage disposal. In this way, by avoiding something she did not want to do, we strengthened her good behaviour. You may have enjoyed negative reinforcements yourself, for example, when a professor allows you to not take the final exam when your grade is high enough; Or allow you to achieve other important goals in the classroom without doing homework. However, negative enhancements were less effective. For example, parents usually use nagging to try to clean their children's rooms. In such cases, the children are forced to clean their rooms in order to avoid being nagging. While this may have an effect, it is not usually pleasant. On the contrary, behaviouralists would recommend that parents create positive reinforcements to motivate children to clean their rooms. By providing meaningful rewards, using the currency economy or using the Premak principle to encourage desired behaviour, you can also change behaviour without suffering the tension associated with nagging or other aversions.

p119.original: 消退可以确保解决问题，但前提是控制了所有强化物。在玛蒂的案例中，消退来自你在她发脾气时不退让，不给她想要的东西。你让她的怒火自己燃烧殆尽。这可能是个挑战，因为这意味着你必须忍受她发脾气。如果她在公共场合发脾气，你可能会尴尬。（你有没有想过为什么孩子们似乎凭直觉就知道要选择在公共场合发脾气？也许是因为他们很快就学到，他们会从恼怒的父母那里得到糖果或关注作为“奖赏”，而父母只是想让孩子停下来，这是另一个滥用负强化的例子！）消退的另一个问题是它可能需要一段时间，所以当消退的应用对象从事着危险的行为——例如，在繁华的路段玩耍时，消退就不是个好选择。
p119.en: Declining ensures that the problem is solved, provided that all enhancements are controlled. In Maddie's case, it comes from the fact that you don't give up when she's angry, and you don't give her what she wants. You let her get angry and burn herself out. This could be a challenge, because it means you have to put up with her anger. If she's angry in public, you might be embarrassed. Do you ever wonder why kids seem to know by instinct that they're going to have to lose their temper in public? Perhaps because they soon learned that they would get candy or attention from their angry parents as a “reward”, and that parents just wanted their children to stop, is another example of abuse of negative reinforcements! Another problem with retreat is that it may take some time, so it is not a good choice when the object of the retreat is engaged in dangerous behaviour — for example, playing in a rich section of the road.

p120.original: 惩罚可能很诱人，但我们已经了解到，它通常会产生我们不想要的效果，例如，攻击或逃避。此外，惩罚往往会破坏惩罚者与被惩罚者之间的关系，并且难以一以贯之地运用。如果你决定因为玛蒂发脾气而惩罚她，那么就让惩罚成为一个合乎逻辑的结果，例如，如果她在家里发脾气，那么就让她“超时”地待在她的房间里，并且惩罚要迅速，却不要过度严厉。
p120.en: Punishment may be tempting, but we have learned that it usually produces effects that we do not want, such as attacks or evasion. Moreover, punishment often undermines the relationship between the punishmenter and the punished person and is difficult to apply consistently. If you decide to punish her for her temperament, then it is a logical consequence, for example, if she is angry at home, then let her stay in her room “over time” and punish quickly, without excessive severity.

p121.original: 你可以做的是结合多种策略。在玛蒂的案例中，这既包括（通过正负强化）强化她的可取行为，也包括对她的不可取行为使用消退或合乎逻辑的后果的策略。我们鼓励你在下次与行为不良的人打交道时自己试试这些策略。请记住，需要改变的可能是你自己的行为！
p121.en: What you can do is combine a variety of strategies. In the case of Marty, this included both reinforcing her desirable behaviour (through positive and negative reinforcement) and using a strategy of regressive or logical consequences for her undesirable behaviour. We encourage you to try these tactics yourself the next time you deal with people who are bad. Remember, it's probably your own behavior that needs to be changed!

p122.original: 4.7 操作性条件反射和经典条件反射的比较
p122.en: 4.7 Comparison of operational and classical reflections

p124.original: 区分操作性条件反射和经典条件反射的过程。
p124.en: The process of distinguishing between operational and classic reflections.

p125.original: 我们已经研究了操作性条件反射和经典条件反射的主要特征，现在让我们来并列比较它们。一般而言，行为的后果——尤其是奖赏和惩罚——将操作性条件反射与经典条件反射区分开来。更具体而言，我们可以关注两种学习类型之间的三个显著差异。
p125.en: We have studied the main features of operational and classical reflections, and now let us compare them in parallel. Generally speaking, the consequences of conduct — in particular rewards and penalties — distinguish between operational and classic conditions. More specifically, we can focus on three significant differences between the two types of learning.

p126.original: 4.7.1 行为反应是在新刺激之前还是之后
p126.en: 4.7.1 Behavior reaction before or after a new stimulus

p127.original: 在经典条件反射中，新刺激是中性刺激，当它与非条件刺激配对时，会引发行为反应。因此，新刺激出现在行为反应之前。然而，在操作性条件反射中，我们在行为反应之后以奖赏或惩罚的形式提供新刺激。因此，区分经典条件反射和操作性条件反射的一种方式是确定行为发生在刺激之前还是之后：如果行为发生在这个过程结束时，我们面临的是经典条件反射；而如果它启动了这个过程，那么这就是操作性条件反射在起作用。
p127.en: In the classic reflections, the new stimulus is a neutral stimulus, which triggers behavioural reactions when paired with non-conditional stimulus. Thus, new incentives appear before behavioural reactions. However, in the reflection of operational conditions, we provide new incentives in the form of rewards or penalties after behavioural reactions. Thus, one way to distinguish between classic and operational reflexes is to determine whether the act occurs before or after the stimulation: if the act occurs at the end of the process, we are faced with classic reflexes; And if it starts this process, then that's how operational conditions reflect.

p128.original: 但请注意，这里有一个潜在混淆点：相同的刺激可以在不同类型的条件反射中发挥不同的作用。所以不要让刺激的性质欺骗了你。如图4-7所示，食物在操作性条件反射中充当奖赏，但在经典条件反射中，食物是一种非条件刺激。需要注意的重要一点是，在经典条件反射中，食物先于行为反应发生，因此不能作为奖赏。然而，在操作性条件反射中，它发生于行为反应之后，因此可以成为奖赏。
p128.en: But note that there is a potential confusion here: the same stimulus can play a different role in reflecting different types of conditions. So don't let the irritation be deceiving you. As shown in figures 4-7, food is a reward for operational reflections, but in classic reflections, food is a non-conditional incentive. It is important to note that in classic reflections, food precedes behavioural reactions and therefore cannot be a reward. However, in the reflection of operational conditions, it occurs after the reaction and can therefore be rewarded.

p129.original: 图4-7 相同的刺激在经典条件反射和操作性条件反射中扮演不同的角色
p129.en: Figure 4-7 The same stimulus plays a different role in classic and operational reflections

p131.original: 举出食物作为刺激的例子
p131.en: Take food as an example of stimulus.

p132.original: 举一个你自己生活中的例子，说明某种食物被用来塑造行为。明确你的例子说明的是经典条件反射还是操作性条件反射。
p132.en: To give an example of your own life, some food is used to shape behavior. It's clear whether your example is classic or operational.

p133.original: 4.7.2 行为是自主的还是反射性的

p134.original: 区分经典条件反射和操作性条件反射的另一种方式是考虑行为本身。它是一种反射性行为吗，例如，分泌唾液、感觉不舒服或与某些其他“内嵌”生物模式相关？如果是，你正在跟经典条件反射打交道，它通常以生物的刺激和反应模式开始（例如，生理情感引发快乐，或巨响引发畏缩或恐惧）。当我们让未能使“内嵌”到生物刺激中的新刺激与生物刺激相伴出现时，学习就会发生，针对新刺激产生同样的旧反应。
p134.en: Another way of distinguishing between classic and operational reflections is to consider the conduct itself. Is it a reflexive behaviour, for example, to saliva, to feel uncomfortable or to be associated with some other “inline” biological pattern? If so, you are dealing with classic retroreflection, which usually starts in the form of biological irritation and reaction (e.g., physical emotion causing happiness, or a loud noise causing fear or fear). When we allow new incentives that fail to “inline” to biostimulate to accompany biostimulate, learning happens, with the same old reaction to new incentives.

p135.original: 相比之下，操作性行为不是基于类似狗的唾液分泌或小阿尔伯特的哭泣一样的自动反射行为。相反，它是一种通过主动选择对奖赏或惩罚做出反应而自主发展出的行为。听命而坐是狗为了获得食物奖赏而做出的选择。为了取得好成绩而学习是你为了获得学业奖赏而做出的选择。因此，经典条件反映通常是非自主和无意识的，而操作性行为是自主和有意识的。套用一句谚语：你可以让狗分泌唾液（一种反射），但你无法强迫它进食（一种操作性行为）。
p135.en: By contrast, the operational behaviour is not an automatic reflection based on a saliva genre similar to that of a dog or a cry of a little Albert. Rather, it is an act that has evolved autonomously by taking the initiative to respond to rewards or penalties. It is the choice of dogs to sit on their orders in order to get food rewards. Learning for good results is the choice you make to get a scholarship. Thus, classic conditions reflect usually non-autonomous and unconscious behaviour, while operational behaviour is autonomous and conscious. Applying the proverb: You can give dogs saliva (a reflection), but you can't force them to eat (an operational act).

p137.original: 这两种条件反射的另一个区别是它们所针对的行为类型（见表4-2）。操作性条件反射鼓励新行为——铺床、上班、养成健康的饮食习惯或学习备考。再者，经典条件反射强调引发对新刺激的旧反应，例如，听到铃声时分泌唾液或听到牙医使用钻头的声音时退缩。因此，在经典条件反射中，行为并无新意，只是将现有行为与新刺激联系起来。
p137.en: Another difference between the reflections of the two conditions is the type of behaviour they address (see tables 4-2). Operational reflection encourages new behaviour - bed-laying, work, healthy eating habits, or learning preparation. Furthermore, classic conditions reflect on the initiation of old reactions to new irritation, for example, when saliva is heard or when dentists are heard using drills. Thus, in the classic reflection of conditions, behaviour is not new, but rather a link between existing behaviour and new incentives.

p138.original: 表4-2 经典条件反射和操作性条件反射的对比
p138.en: Table 4-2 Comparison of classic and operational reflections

p139.original: 你可能还注意到，消退在两种学习形式中的作用也略有不同。在经典条件反射中，消退需要让非条件刺激不出现，这样就切断了两种刺激之间的联系。而在操作性条件反射中，消退是由让强化物不出现而导致的，因为没有奖赏或惩罚，就没有理由执行该行为。
p139.en: You may also note that there is a slight difference in the role played by retreat in the two forms of learning. In the classic reflection of conditions, the need for absconding non-conditional incentives would cut off the link between the two. In operational reflections, the retreat is caused by the absence of the reinforcement, since there is no reason to carry out the act without rewards or penalties.

p141.original: 但是，不要错误地认为经典条件反射和操作性条件反射对学习的解释是相互对立的，它们可以互补。事实上，最初由经典条件反射学到的反应通常会随着时间的推移通过操作性条件反射得到维持。这是如何发生的呢？以蛇恐怖症为例，假设对蛇的恐惧最初是通过经典条件反射习得的，当时蛇（条件刺激）与令人惊恐的非条件刺激配对（有人大喊“小心”）。一旦建立了恐惧反应，它就可以通过操作性条件反射来维持和加强。每当你回避恐惧对象时，你焦虑的减少都会成为回避行为的负强化物（即正性结果），从而进一步强化了恐怖症。你还可能从附近的朋友或家人那里获得安慰或关注的正强化（见图4-8）。
p141.en: However, it is not wrong to assume that classic and operational reflections of conditions are mutually opposing interpretations of learning, and that they complement each other. In fact, responses initially learned from classic reflections are usually sustained over time by operational reflections. How did this happen? In the case of snake terror, it is assumed that fear of snakes was initially reflected in classic conditions, when snakes (conditional irritation) were matched by alarming non-conditional irritation (some shouted “caution”). Once a fear response is established, it can be maintained and strengthened through operational conditions. Every time you avoid fear, your anxiety is reduced as a negative reinforcement (i.e., a positive result) of the circumvention, thus further exacerbating the symptoms of terror. You may also be receiving consolation or increased concern from friends or family members in the vicinity (see figures 4-8).

p142.original: 图4-8 经典条件反射和操作性条件反射可以共同起作用
p142.en: Figure 4-8 Classic and operational conditions reflect together

p143.original: 注：最初通过经典条件反射习得的反应可以通过操作性强化来维持和加强。
p143.en: Note: The response initially obtained through classic conditions reflections can be sustained and strengthened through operational reinforcement.

p144.original: 心理学很有用 运用心理学来学习心理学
p144.en: Psychology is useful. Use psychology to learn psychology.

p145.original: 你可能已经尝试过，用普雷马克原则来鼓励自己多学习，例如，在完成家庭作业之前不看电视，不去冰箱里拿东西。它适用于某些人，但如果它不适合你，请尝试让学习本身更有趣，更有回报。
p145.en: You may have tried to encourage yourself to learn more by using the Premak principle, for example, not to watch TV until you finish your homework, not to pick up anything in the fridge. It applies to some people, but if it doesn't suit you, try to make learning itself more interesting and rewarding.

p146.original: 对于我们大多数人来说，无论做什么，与我们喜欢的人聚在一起都是一种强化。所以，可以尝试让你的某些（而不是全部）学习成为一项社交活动。例如，安排一个时间，让你可以与一两个同学聚在一起确认和讨论重要的概念，并尝试预测下一次测试的内容。
p146.en: For most of us, it is an intensification of what we do and what we like to do. So you can try to make some, not all, of your studies a social event. For example, a time has been allocated to allow you to come together with one or two classmates to identify and discuss important concepts and try to predict the content of the next test.

p147.original: 并且不要只关注专业词汇。相反，尝试发现全景——探寻本章每一节的整体含义。核心概念是一个很好的起点。然后，你可以和你的朋友们讨论细节。你很可能会发现，即将到来的学习小组带给你的社会压力（作为间歇强化物）将有助于激励你完成阅读并找出模糊不懂的地方。当你们聚在一起参加小组学习时，你会发现解释你所学的知识可以加强你自己的理解。通过这种方式，你可以从一系列强化措施中受益：与朋友共度时光、学得更好以及在考试中取得更好的成绩。
p147.en: And don't just focus on professional vocabulary. Instead, an attempt is made to discover the landscape — to explore the overall meaning of each section of this chapter. The core concept is a good starting point. Then you can discuss the details with your friends. And you're very likely to find that the social pressure brought to you by the upcoming study group (as an intermittent reinforcement) will help motivate you to complete your reading and to find a place that you don't understand. When you come together to study in groups, you will find that explaining the knowledge you have learned can strengthen your own understanding. In this way, you can benefit from a series of intensive measures: spending time with friends, learning better, and achieving better results in exams.
